name: Chang Pi
bio: Chang Pi is dated by Giles to the 10th century AD. His poem here is addressed to an absent love.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: To an Absent Fair One
poems.author: Chang Pi
poems.text:
After parting, dreams possessed me and I wandered you know where,
And we sat in the verandah and you sang. the sweet old air.
Then I woke, with no one near me save the moon still shining on,
And lighting up dead petals which like you have passed and gone.

poems.title: A Message
poems.author: Chang Pi
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
I go in a dream to the house of Hsieh —
Through a zigzag porch with arching rails
To a court where the spring moon lights for ever
Phantom flowers and a single figure.

poems.title: 寄人 (Ji ren)
poems.author: Chang Pi
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
別夢依依到謝家，小廊回合曲闌斜。
多情只有春庭月，猶爲離人照落花。
